title: Amazon Stock (AMZN) Falls 1.4% After Q3 Earnings Report (Oct 30)
summary: Amazon stock (AMZN) fell 1.41% to $240.35 on Oct 30 after Q3 earnings and revenue came in below estimates, while AWS sales grew 39%.
body_markdown:
Among other large technology names,[Microsoft (MSFT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/msft/) fell 1.55%,[Meta Platforms (META)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/meta/) lost 1.53% and[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) declined 1.40%. Amazon closed 16.31% below its 52-week high of $287.20 and 22.63% above its 52-week low of $196.00.


## Why Amazon Stock Fell


Amazon published its third-quarter[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) after the market closed on October 29. According to the[company's official release](https://s2.q4cdn.com/299287126/files/doc_earnings/2026/q3/earnings-result/AMZN-Q3-2026-Earnings-Release.pdf) , net sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion and operating income climbed to $28.1 billion from $17.4 billion, a 13.9% operating margin that Amazon called its highest ever. Net income fell to $20.7 billion, or $1.89 per diluted share, from $1.95 a year earlier, which the company attributed mainly to $9.5 billion of pre-tax gains on its Anthropic investments in the prior-year quarter.


Per the Illawarra Mercury report, analysts had expected $1.97 per share and $202.2 billion in revenue, citing FactSet. Amazon guided to fourth-quarter net sales of $240.0 billion to $247.0 billion, and the report noted that the midpoint of that range sits below the $244.16 billion analysts expected.


Amazon also said Prime Day shifted into the second quarter for most large countries this year, and that third-quarter sales growth would have been about 400 basis points higher without that shift.


## AMZN Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- AWS sales rose 39% to $46.0 billion and AWS operating income reached $17.8 billion, up from $11.4 billion, per the release. CEO Andy Jassy projected AWS revenue growth of over 40% in both 2027 and 2028, a company projection.
- [24/7 Wall St.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/amazon-stock-fell-earnings-jim-220705519.html) reported that the AWS backlog rose to $578 billion.
- Amazon guided to fourth-quarter operating income of $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion, compared with $25.0 billion a year earlier, and said it expects advertising revenue to grow in the high teens in the quarter.


### Risks


- Free cash flow for the trailing twelve months turned into an outflow of $42.4 billion, driven mainly by a $94.8 billion rise in purchases of property and equipment tied largely to AI, according to the release. Amazon still expects 2026 cash capital spending of about $220 billion.
- Per 24/7 Wall St., management expects meaningfully higher spending in 2027, interest expense rose to $1.691 billion from $538 million a year earlier, and UBS analyst Stephen Ju said investors feared 2027 capital spending could exceed $300 billion.
- [TIKR](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/anthropic-reduplicating-aws-rents-own-074652977.html) noted that Anthropic now leases its own data centers, which it argued could cap further AWS gains from Anthropic beyond the $110 billion Anthropic has committed to AWS through 2036.
